40	// AttachKind selects what kind of attach should happen for the
41	// state-tagging helper AttachSession.
42	type AttachKind int
43	
44	const (
45		// AttachKindReview tags the session as an agent_review.
46		AttachKindReview AttachKind = iota
47	
48		// AttachKindInvestigate tags the session as an agent_investigate.
49		AttachKindInvestigate
50	)
51	
52	// String returns the session.Kind value AttachKind would set on state.
53	// Used for error messages so users see the same kind names that appear
54	// in stored state files.
55	func (k AttachKind) String() string {
56		switch k {
57		case AttachKindReview:
58			return string(session.KindAgentReview)
59		case AttachKindInvestigate:
60			return string(session.KindAgentInvestigate)
61		default:
62			return fmt.Sprintf("attach-kind(%d)", int(k))
63		}
64	}
65	
66	// AttachOptions parameterizes AttachSession.
67	//
68	// Kind selects which set of fields is meaningful:
69	//   - AttachKindReview reads ReviewSkills and ReviewPrompt.
70	//   - AttachKindInvestigate reads InvestigateRunID/Round/Turn/Topic/Prompt.
71	//
72	// AttachSession is a state-only tagger: it does not read the transcript,
73	// create checkpoints, or amend commits. Use runAttach for the full
74	// transcript+checkpoint flow; AttachSession is for retroactively marking
75	// a session that's already tracked.
76	type AttachOptions struct {
77		SessionID string
78		Kind      AttachKind
79	
80		// Review-only fields (used when Kind == AttachKindReview).
81		ReviewSkills []string
82		ReviewPrompt string
83	
84		// Investigate-only fields (used when Kind == AttachKindInvestigate).
85		InvestigateRunID  string
86		InvestigateRound  int
87		InvestigateTurn   int
88		InvestigateTopic  string
89		InvestigatePrompt string
90	}
91	
92	// AttachSession tags an existing session as the specified Kind.
93	//
94	// Behavior:
95	//   - The session must already be tracked (state file present); a missing
96	//     session returns "session %q not found".
97	//   - Tagging is idempotent for the same Kind: re-tagging overwrites the
98	//     kind-specific fields (skills/prompt for review, run-id/round/turn/
99	//     topic/prompt for investigate) and leaves state.Kind unchanged.
100	//   - Cross-kind retagging is rejected: a session marked as one Kind
101	//     cannot be retagged as a different Kind ("session %q is already
102	//     tagged as %s; cannot retag as %s").
103	func AttachSession(ctx context.Context, opts AttachOptions) error {
104		if opts.SessionID == "" {
105			return errors.New("AttachSession: SessionID is required")
106		}
107	
108		store, err := session.NewStateStore(ctx)
109		if err != nil {
110			return fmt.Errorf("failed to open session store: %w", err)
111		}
112		state, err := store.Load(ctx, opts.SessionID)
113		if err != nil {
114			return fmt.Errorf("failed to load session state: %w", err)
115		}
116		if state == nil {
117			return fmt.Errorf("session %q not found", opts.SessionID)
118		}
119	
120		desiredKind := attachKindToSessionKind(opts.Kind)
121		if state.Kind != "" && state.Kind != desiredKind {
122			return fmt.Errorf(
123				"session %q is already tagged as %s; cannot retag as %s",
124				opts.SessionID, string(state.Kind), desiredKind,
125			)
126		}
127	
128		switch opts.Kind {
129		case AttachKindReview:
130			state.Kind = session.KindAgentReview
131			state.ReviewSkills = opts.ReviewSkills
132			state.ReviewPrompt = opts.ReviewPrompt
133		case AttachKindInvestigate:
134			state.Kind = session.KindAgentInvestigate
135			state.InvestigateRunID = opts.InvestigateRunID
136			state.InvestigateRound = opts.InvestigateRound
137			state.InvestigateTurn = opts.InvestigateTurn
138			state.InvestigateTopic = opts.InvestigateTopic
139			state.InvestigatePrompt = opts.InvestigatePrompt
140		default:
141			return fmt.Errorf("AttachSession: unknown attach kind %d", int(opts.Kind))
142		}
143	
144		if err := store.Save(ctx, state); err != nil {
145			return fmt.Errorf("failed to save session state: %w", err)
146		}
147		return nil
148	}
149	
150	// attachKindToSessionKind translates an AttachKind into the corresponding
151	// session.Kind value. Kept private so callers go through AttachSession.
152	func attachKindToSessionKind(k AttachKind) session.Kind {
153		switch k {
154		case AttachKindReview:
155			return session.KindAgentReview
156		case AttachKindInvestigate:
157			return session.KindAgentInvestigate
158		default:
159			return ""
160		}
161	}
162	
163	// attachReviewSession is a thin compatibility wrapper around AttachSession
164	// for the review-only path. New callers should prefer AttachSession.
165	func attachReviewSession(ctx context.Context, sessionID string, skills []string, prompt string) error {
166		return AttachSession(ctx, AttachOptions{
167			SessionID:    sessionID,
168			Kind:         AttachKindReview,
169			ReviewSkills: skills,
170			ReviewPrompt: prompt,
171		})
172	}
173	
174	// attachOptions carries optional flags for runAttach. Force is the original
175	// flag; Review opts the attach into recording the session as an
176	// agent_review in the checkpoint metadata.
177	type attachOptions struct {
178		Force bool
179		// Review, when true, tags the attached session as a review. Skills are
180		// resolved inside runAttach after the real agent is known (via session
181		// state or transcript auto-detection), not at the cobra layer — the
182		// --agent flag's default points at claude-code, which would otherwise
183		// make a Gemini session incorrectly look up review.claude-code config.
184		Review bool
185		// ReviewSkillsOverride, when non-empty, declares which review skills were
186		// run. Empty is valid: the session is still tagged as a review, with no
187		// structured skills list. Ignored when Review=false.
188		ReviewSkillsOverride []string
189		// ReviewPromptOverride, when non-empty, is recorded instead of the
190		// transcript's first user prompt. Used by `entire review attach` when a
191		// pending-review marker has the exact prompt the user was asked to run.
192		ReviewPromptOverride string
193	}

19	// ComposeInput is the per-turn data needed to render an investigate prompt.
20	//
21	// The struct is intentionally kept narrow: the loop driver passes only what
22	// the prompt template uses. Marvin's prompt also surfaces prior decisions,
23	// claims, and fixes from its memory store; entire does not have an
24	// equivalent surface yet, so callers may pass arbitrary text via
25	// PriorContext (e.g. checkpoint search excerpts) for rendering.
26	type ComposeInput struct {
27		// Topic is the human-readable subject of the investigation. Used in
28		// the body of the prompt as plain text — never as a section heading,
29		// since the rendered findings doc owns that.
30		Topic string
31	
32		// AgentName is the agent the prompt is being rendered for (e.g.

34		AgentName string

git add -u && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
investigate: drop --topic flag and investigate attach; rename picker prompt

Three connected changes:

1. Remove the --topic flag entirely. With it gone, an investigation can
   start from (a) a positional [seed-doc] path, (b) --issue-link, or
   (c) the spawn-time multipicker's "Investigation prompt" field — which
   now becomes the topic when no seed/issue was supplied. The
   multipicker form's field is labelled "Investigation prompt" instead
   of "Optional per-run prompt", and is only shown when no seed-doc /
   --issue-link is set.

   PickInvestigateAgents grows an askPrompt bool parameter so callers
   can suppress the prompt form when the topic is already known from
   seed/issue. PickedInvestigate.PerRun → PickedInvestigate.Prompt to
   match the new role.

2. Remove the `entire investigate attach <session-id>` subcommand.
   The top-level `entire attach` only supports --review, so this kill
   also lets us collapse the now-single-valued AttachKind machinery in
   cli/attach.go: the AttachKind enum, attachKindToSessionKind,
   AttachKindInvestigate, the Investigate-only fields on AttachOptions,
   and the dead attachReviewSession wrapper all go.

3. Drop the dormant PriorEntireContextFn / PriorEntireContext /
   PriorContext / composeAlwaysPrompt chain. The picker's prompt now
   IS the topic when shown, so the "append per-run preamble to
   AlwaysPrompt" path has no source. PriorEntireContextFn was always
   wired nil in production and only existed as scaffolding for a
   hypothetical future "wire `entire search` into the seed" feature
   that's no longer planned (agents are instructed to use
   `entire search` themselves via the per-turn prompt).

Removed files: cmd/entire/cli/investigate/attach.go +
attach_test.go, cmd/entire/cli/attach_investigate_test.go,
cmd/entire/cli/investigate/testdata/prompt-with-prior-context.txt.
Removed integration test: TestInvestigateAttach_*.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Committed as `05bb259d8`. Net: **+132 / -1112** across 19 files.

Summary of changes:

**Picker (`multipicker.go`):**
- `PickInvestigateAgents(ctx, eligible, askPrompt bool)` — new bool gate.
- `askPrompt=true` (no seed/issue) → shows form labelled **"Investigation prompt"** with description "Describe what you want investigated — this becomes the topic for the run."
- `askPrompt=false` (seed or --issue-link supplied) → prompt form skipped entirely.
- `PickedInvestigate.PerRun` → `PickedInvestigate.Prompt`.

**`--topic` removed:**
- Flag, runFlags field, validation cases, resolveTopicAndSeed branch, Long help text — all gone.
- `resolveTopicAndSeed` now takes a `pickerPrompt` argument; when no seed/issue, the picker prompt becomes the topic.

**`investigate attach` removed:**
- Deleted: `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/attach.go`, `attach_test.go`, `cmd/entire/cli/attach_investigate_test.go`, integration test `TestInvestigateAttach_*`.
- Collapsed cli/attach.go: dropped `AttachKind` enum + `attachKindToSessionKind` + `AttachKindInvestigate` + Investigate-only fields on `AttachOptions` + unused `attachReviewSession` wrapper.
- Dropped `Deps.AttachCmd`, `newInvestigateAttachCmd`, the conditional `cmd.AddCommand(deps.AttachCmd)`.
- `buildInvestigateDeps()` no longer takes a `*cobra.Command`.

**Dead-code sweep:**
- `PriorEntireContextFn` Dep + `PriorEntireContext` BootstrapInput field + scaffold's "## Prior Entire Context" block + `priorSection` template var.
- `LoopInput.PriorContext` + `ComposeInput.PriorContext` + prompt's `## Prior context` block.
- `composeAlwaysPrompt` helper.
- Stale `--topic` comment refs.

Build, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` all clean. Tests pass except for the pre-existing unrelated `TestReviewSummaryTokenEnricher_LoadsCurrentSessionState` failure.

content.text:
# Simplify: Code Review and Cleanup

Review all changed files for reuse, quality, and efficiency. Fix any issues found.

## Phase 1: Identify Changes

Run `git diff` (or `git diff HEAD` if there are staged changes) to see what changed. If there are no git changes, review the most recently modified files that the user mentioned or that you edited earlier in this conversation.

## Phase 2: Launch Three Review Agents in Parallel

Use the Agent tool to launch all three agents concurrently in a single message. Pass each agent the full diff so it has the complete context.

### Agent 1: Code Reuse Review

For each change:

1. **Search for existing utilities and helpers** that could replace newly written code. Look for similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase — common locations are utility directories, shared modules, and files adjacent to the changed ones.
2. **Flag any new function that duplicates existing functionality.** Suggest the existing function to use instead.
3. **Flag any inline logic that could use an existing utility** — hand-rolled string manipulation, manual path handling, custom environment checks, ad-hoc type guards, and similar patterns are common candidates.

### Agent 2: Code Quality Review

Review the same changes for hacky patterns:

1. **Redundant state**: state that duplicates existing state, cached values that could be derived, observers/effects that could be direct calls
2. **Parameter sprawl**: adding new parameters to a function instead of generalizing or restructuring existing ones

# Investigate-loop efficiency review

## HIGH

**1. `findings.md` SHA-256'd twice per turn — O(turns² · size) work** `cmd/entire/cli/investigate/loop.go:260,307` (`hashFile` at 518). Findings grow each turn; with 12 turns and a 50KB final doc the loop reads ~325KB of cumulative bytes through SHA-256. Real cost is small but the pattern scales quadratically. **Fix:** `PlanChanged` only needs a change signal — replace `hashFile` with `os.Stat` returning `(size, mtime, ok)` and compare the tuple. Free, equally correct. Keep SHA only if you ever need cross-machine content equality.

**2. TUI ticker rebuilds the entire frame at 10 Hz even when nothing is running** `tui_model.go:147` (`tickCmd` every 100 ms) + `Update` at line 180 dispatches `tickCmd` unconditionally on every `tickMsg`, and `View()` rebuilds all rows + duration math every frame (`dashboardView` at 400, `formatRowDuration` at 529). Between turns (most of an agent run — agents take seconds-to-minutes per turn), no row has `currentStart` set, so the redraw is pure noise. **Fix:** gate the tick on "any row has `currentStart != zero`". When no row is running, return only `spinCmd` from the tick handler; restart the ticker in `handleTurnStarted`. Or drop to a 500 ms tick — the spinner stays fluid at that rate and View work drops 5x.

## MEDIUM

**3. `List` + parse-every-file fan-out for callers that want one manifest** `manifest.go:141`. `show.go:54` and `clean.go:59` call `List` then resolve a single run id (exact / prefix match). For exact-match `RunID`, `FindByRunID` already exists (Glob-based) and is the right tool. **Fix:** in `show.RunShow` and `clean.selectCleanTargets`, when `RunID` is set, try `FindByRunID` first; fall back to `List` only when the user supplied a prefix (no exact match). Eliminates N-file parse for the most common "I know the id" case. `findings.go:34` legitimately needs all manifests (it renders the full list).

**4. `migration.go` re-reads project settings JSON on every invocation** `migration.go:76-105`. Cheap (~few KB), but it runs unconditionally even when the file has no `investigate` key (steady state forever after one migration). **Fix:** before opening the file, check `settings.Load()`'s already-cached object for a non-nil `Investigate` field; only open the raw JSON when the cached settings indicate the legacy key is still there. Or skip entirely — once #1009 ships, this self-extinguishes per-repo. Low-stakes; flag-only.

## LOW

**5. `AppendInvestigateEnv` scans `os.Environ()` × `IsEntry`** `env.go:62-68` calling `provenance.IsEntry` (`provenance/env.go:73`) which does two `hasAnyPrefix` calls = 15 string-prefix comparisons per entry. ~1500 ops/turn at typical env sizes. Absolute cost is microseconds; not worth fixing. If you ever do, the natural shape is a single switch on the `ENTIRE_` prefix before the per-name check.

**6. `runFresh` sequential `WorktreeRoot` + `currentHeadSHA`** `cmd.go:630,634`. Both fast (single git operation each). Parallelising buys nothing measurable; benchmark would not justify the goroutine + errgroup overhead. **Skip.**

**7. Spawned-process cleanup on cancel** `loop.go:304` uses `cmd.Run()`; all three spawners (`agent/codex/spawner.go:34`, `claudecode/spawner.go:31`, `geminicli/spawner.go:24`) use `exec.CommandContext`. On ctx cancel, the runtime kills the child and `cmd.Run()` returns. No leak. The ctx-cancel check at `loop.go:189` happens before `runOneTurn`, so a kill mid-turn surfaces as `runErr` and gets recorded as a failed stance. **Clean.**

**8. TUI goroutine lifecycle** `tui_sink.go:64-72`. Single goroutine, `defer close(s.done)` covers panic-through-recover paths inside `tea.Program.Run`. `RunFinished` always calls `Wait()` (line 125). No early-return path in the loop bypasses `RunFinished` (it's called on every terminal branch in `RunInvestigateLoop`). **Clean.**

**9. `agentRow.buffer` memory** `tui_model.go:228,270`. Two appends per turn × `maxTurns` × agents. With defaults (`maxTurns=2`, 3 agents) = 12 entries total. Even at maxTurns=10 with 5 agents that's 100 small structs. **Clean.**

**10. State.json reload between turns** `loop.go:333` calls `store.Load` which reads + unmarshals the whole file — but the file is tiny (single-run state, KB-scale). Necessary because agent rewrites it. No other per-turn re-reads of manifest/settings/findings outside the two `hashFile` calls already flagged in #1. **Clean.**

**Net recommended changes:** stat-tuple instead of SHA in `hashFile` (#1); gate tick on running rows (#2); short-circuit single-id `show`/`clean` through `FindByRunID` (#3). Everything else either won't move the needle or is already correct.

investigate: drive PlanChanged from stat tuple, not findings SHA

The loop signalled "did this turn change the findings doc" by SHA-256'ing
findings.md before and after each agent run. As findings grow across a
run, this is O(turns² · size) bytes hashed for no upgrade in signal
quality — PlanChanged only needs a change detector, not content equality.

Replace hashFile with fileFingerprint returning "<size>:<unix-nanos
mtime>". The agent process runs for wall-clock seconds-to-minutes between
the pre and post stat, so mtime always ticks when the file is rewritten.
Drops the crypto/sha256, encoding/hex, and io.Copy machinery; same
correctness.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
